answer: Each identity locks a 75-credit bond and registers one karst terrace weir. The keeper pays a fee, logs terrace flow each tide, and posts the weir key. An auditor recomputes discharge from weir width and tide height, and burns the bond when a reading, key, or tide entry mismatches, repeats, or goes missing. The first weir costs 30 credits; the kth costs 30+6(k-1), so the 1000th costs 6024, and 1000 fake identities pay 3,027,000 in fees plus 75,000 locked. An honest keeper pays 30 once. A rented-weir ring fails because the rented weir is already registered, so its duplicate log exposes both.
